reasons: Cited Section 17(b) gives the Customer (Sparkling) an unconditional at-will termination right on 90 days' written notice, which sits squarely within the fallback window (60–90 days), with no early-termination fee, penalty or non-refundability charge in the quoted text.
Vendor (Garman) has no convenience right — its termination triggers in p0128 are insolvency/uncured material default — so the walk-away scenario (Vendor convenience on short notice) is not engaged.

Shortfalls versus preferred (90 rather than 30 days' notice; silence on pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) exit) are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is plausibly a keyword false negative — the clause grants an unconditional 'at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice' right without using the phrase 'for convenience' — and does not undermine the substantive analysis.
